clauses.clause: OTel does not replace logging libraries; Logs API primarily for appender authors
Two collection paths: file/stdout via Collector filelog, or direct-to-collector OTLP
clauses.note: Non-OTLP JSON/text sink path acknowledged; Collector filelog ingestion route never named as an alternative owner.

clauses.clause: Log source categories; system/infra logs get Resource enrichment only, trace correlation infeasible
clauses.note: Skills scope is first-party application logging paths only.

clauses.clause: New first-party apps: logging library + appender, or Logs API directly
clauses.note: Skills mandate the bridge route; direct Logs API use for structured events is never offered as an alternative.

clauses.clause: Collector enriches all signals uniformly without application change
Auto-instrumenting existing logging to inject trace IDs is possible in some languages
No universal official list of what to log; scoped guidance only (S7 when-to-define-events, S8 exceptions, domain conventions)
clauses.normative: mixed; most S7 clauses bind semconv authors
clauses.note: Covered by correct omission: skills invent no universal business-event list; coverage is path/scenario-driven and domain guidance is kept in separately scoped references.

clauses.clause: API SHOULD provide global default LoggerProvider set/register/access
clauses.note: SDK-author obligation; LR:25-27 states the principle that such clauses are not automatically missing application code.

clauses.clause: Get a Logger MUST accept name + optional version/schema_url/attributes; source logger name should be recorded as scope name
clauses.note: Scope name is asserted in proof; the mapping rule from source logger name is only implied by 'logger/scope'.

clauses.clause: Logger MUST provide Emit; all record params optional incl. EventName; implicit Context optional and MUST use current, explicit Context SHOULD be required
clauses.note: Captured per language (Go InfoContext/ErrorContext) rather than as a general API rule; sufficient.

clauses.clause: API MAY accept an Exception parameter
Logger SHOULD provide Enabled; MUST return boolean; value not static and can become stale
Optional params MUST be accepted but MUST NOT be obligated
LoggerProvider and Logger methods MUST be documented safe for concurrent use
Languages MAY provide ergonomic API favouring event semantics
Two field kinds: top-level named fields vs attribute collections of AnyValue
Timestamp = occurrence time at source, uint64 ns since epoch, optional
ObservedTimestamp = collection time; SHOULD be set once observed; prefer Timestamp when both exist
TraceId/SpanId/TraceFlags per W3C, all optional; if SpanId present TraceId SHOULD be present
SeverityText = original source string, optional
SeverityNumber optional; ranges 1-24; 0 MAY mean unspecified
Source severity must define its mapping; single matching level takes smallest value of range
Severity >= 17 indicates error; do not invent ERROR where source has no severity concept beyond the recommendation
Reverse mapping, display short names, compare via SeverityNumber
Body is AnyValue; MUST support AnyValue to preserve structured-log semantics; field optional
Resource describes source; SHOULD follow resource semconv; optional
InstrumentationScope field, optional
Attributes carry per-occurrence info other than trace context fields; optional
Exceptions MAY be in Attributes; if included MUST follow exception semconv
EventName identifies event class; SHOULD uniquely identify the structure; non-empty name makes the record an Event
Semconv-defined logs SHOULD be Events, but it is NOT a requirement that all LogRecords are Events
clauses.note: LR mirrors the explicit non-requirement precisely: EventName is 'not a mandatory field on ordinary application messages'.

clauses.clause: All language implementations MUST provide an SDK
LoggerProvider MUST allow a Resource; SHOULD associate it with all records
clauses.note: Skills require preserving the existing provider's resource rather than constructing a new provider.

clauses.clause: SDK SHOULD allow multiple independent LoggerProviders
clauses.note: Capability exists in the spec but the skills deliberately forbid adding a second provider; that is a repo policy layered on top of a SHOULD, stated as such.

clauses.clause: Logger creation only via provider; MUST build InstrumentationScope; invalid name MUST still return a working Logger and SHOULD log a message
clauses.note: SDK-author fallback behaviour; an application audit cannot act on it.

clauses.clause: Configuration MUST be provider-owned; updates MUST apply to already-returned Loggers
LoggerConfigurator computes LoggerConfig per scope; helpers MAY select/disable by name, set minimum severity, enable trace-based filtering
LoggerConfig: enabled SHOULD default true (disabled = No-op); minimum_severity MUST default 0 and severity-0 records bypass it; trace_based MUST default false and drops unsampled-trace records
clauses.note: trace_based is named with its correct default and treated as a capability to inspect rather than require; enabled and minimum_severity are absent.

clauses.clause: If ObservedTimestamp unspecified, implementation SHOULD set it to current time

SDK MUST by default set exception semconv attributes from a provided Exception; user-provided attributes MUST take precedence and MUST NOT be overwritten; SDKs MAY consider limits for large stacktraces
clauses.note: Use of the bridge/SDK exception mapping is required and raw-object serialization forbidden, but the user-attribute precedence rule is never stated.

clauses.clause: Filtering order before processing: enabled, then minimum_severity, then trace_based, each a MUST drop
Enabled MUST return false with no processors, when disabled, below minimum severity, trace_based+unsampled, or when all processors return false
Trace context fields MUST be populated from the resolved Context (explicit or current) when emitted; dropped-attribute counts MUST be available to exporters
ReadWriteLogRecord mutable fields; SDK MAY provide deep clone for asynchronous processors to avoid races
clauses.note: Only relevant where a custom processor exists; conditional applicability.

clauses.clause: LogRecord attributes MUST adhere to common limits; SDK MUST provide a way to change them; LogRecordLimits naming; discard message MUST be printed at most once per LogRecord
clauses.note: Limit configuration strongly covered; only the once-per-record diagnostic rule is absent.

clauses.clause: Processors invoked in registration order; each pipeline MAY end in its own exporter; custom and decorated processors MUST be allowed
clauses.note: Skills require preserving existing processors rather than reasoning about ordering.

clauses.clause: OnEmit is called synchronously on the emitting thread and SHOULD NOT block or throw; mutations MUST be visible to later processors; record is not required to be concurrent-safe
clauses.note: The emitting-thread property is exactly why a bridge placed after a logging queue observes the queue worker's context; the skills cover that consequence in all four languages.

clauses.clause: Processor Enabled is MAY; defaults to true when indeterminate; OnEmit must filter independently
Processor Shutdown once per instance; later OnEmit ignored gracefully; Shutdown MUST include the effects of ForceFlush; SHOULD complete or abort within a timeout
ForceFlush: built-ins MUST Export then ForceFlush; MUST prioritize honoring a specified timeout over finishing all calls; SHOULD only be called when absolutely necessary
clauses.note: Skills correctly separate processor wait, exporter attempt and caller lifecycle deadlines and warn that a flush wait is not cancellation or acceptance proof.

clauses.clause: Simple and batch processors MUST both be implemented; other processing SHOULD first be considered out-of-process in the Collector
clauses.note: Batch-processor use is mandated; the 'prefer the Collector for advanced processing' preference is never surfaced, which is the same root as GAP-3.

clauses.clause: Simple and batch processors MUST synchronize calls to the exporter's Export
Batch processor defaults: maxQueueSize 2048 (logs dropped when full), scheduledDelayMillis 1000, exportTimeoutMillis 30000, maxExportBatchSize 512 and <= queue size
clauses.note: Batch<=queue invariant and bounded-queue loss both explicit; 'SDK defaults can be suitable' is stated so a default is not reported as a gap.

clauses.clause: Event-to-span-event bridge processor: SHOULD be provided; bridges only when EventName non-empty, valid TraceId/SpanId, current recording span with matching IDs; exactly one span event; MUST NOT prevent normal pipeline processing
clauses.note: Conditional on SDK support. Relevant to duplicate analysis because the record must still continue down the pipeline.

clauses.clause: Export MUST NOT block indefinitely and MUST time out with Failure; retry and concurrency are the exporter's responsibility and default processors SHOULD NOT implement retry; Failure means the batch must be dropped
clauses.note: The skills' separation of per-attempt vs whole-export budget matches this split of responsibility between processor and exporter.

clauses.clause: Exporter ForceFlush/Shutdown; after Shutdown Export SHOULD return Failure; Shutdown SHOULD NOT block indefinitely
Provider Logger-creation/ForceFlush/Shutdown, all Logger methods, and exporter ForceFlush/Shutdown MUST be concurrency-safe
Logs SDK SHOULD support SDK self-observability
clauses.note: Development-maturity SDK-author obligation; not an application-audit item.

clauses.clause: AnyValue definition; APIs SHOULD document array/map overhead; empty, zero, empty-string and empty-array values are meaningful and MUST be stored and passed on
map<string,AnyValue> unique case-sensitive keys; uniqueness MUST be enforced by default; duplicate-allowing option MAY exist and MUST be documented as unpredictable
Attribute key MUST be non-null non-empty string; value MUST be an AnyValue; keys case-sensitive
Attribute Collections are distinct from map<string,AnyValue> used in attribute values and the log record body; unique keys MUST be enforced by default; same-key set SHOULD overwrite
clauses.note: The collection-vs-nested-map distinction is what makes the Body exclusion in E6 meaningful, and LR:227-231 reflects it.

clauses.clause: SDK SHOULD apply truncation by default; value-length limit MUST truncate strings per character and byte arrays per byte, recursively across arrays and maps; count limit MUST discard excess and applies only to top-level attributes; depth limit replaces deeper arrays/maps with an empty value; MUST provide programmatic change
clauses.note: LR:227-229 explicitly covers byte-array units and recursive array/map value/depth handling and tells the reader to inspect that capability rather than assume every SDK enforces it.

clauses.clause: Limits apply only to attribute collections; value length and depth limits do NOT apply to values within other structures such as LogRecord.Body
clauses.note: Repeated in the common rules and in all four language guides; Body policy is consistently kept separate from attribute limits.

clauses.clause: Defaults AttributeCountLimit 128, AttributeValueLengthLimit Infinity, AttributeValueDepthLimit 64
clauses.note: P:903-912 works a concrete 128/64 env vs 8/32 selected-limit example, including the 'preserve the independent authorized 128/64 policy' instruction.

clauses.clause: Model-specific limit takes precedence over the general limit, then model-specific default, then global default
clauses.note: P:890-894 states the generic/log-specific fallback relationship explicitly, including that OTEL_LOGRECORD_* can override generic constructor arguments.

clauses.clause: Resource attributes SHOULD be exempt from attribute limits; metric attributes exempt at this time
clauses.note: Covered indirectly: resource preservation is mandated and resource is never treated as subject to log attribute limits.

clauses.clause: Non-OTLP representation of AnyValue/Attribute/Attribute Collection via JSON-shaped encoding; explicitly lossy
clauses.note: Exporter-internal encoding; the skills' non-OTLP concern is trace-context fields (F1/F2), which is covered.

clauses.clause: Instrumentation scope is the (name, version, schema_url, attributes) tuple and SHOULD uniquely identify the emitting unit; S4 adds that appenders should avoid setting scope attributes because differing attributes on the same Logger identity is an error
Non-OTLP export MUST report otel.scope.name/version and MUST also report deprecated otel.library.* aliases with identical values
Dropped attributes count MUST be reported as otel.dropped_attributes_count, only when non-zero
clauses.note: Skills require drop accounting 'where supported' rather than assuming the field, which is the correct treatment of an exporter-owned mechanism.

clauses.clause: Non-OTLP formats should use trace_id / span_id (lowercase hex) and trace_flags (W3C traceflags format); all three fields are optional
clauses.note: LR:140-143 also makes the inverse point that attributes merely named trace_id/span_id are not the canonical OTLP fields, which is the distinction this clause depends on.

clauses.clause: Syslog RFC5424 via SD-ID 'OpenTelemetry'; plain text per format custom; JSON as top-level fields; other structured formats as top-level attributes
clauses.note: The JSON/text top-level requirement is covered ('customary top-level trace_id, span_id, trace_flags representation'); the Syslog SD-ID form is never named. Applicability is conditional on a syslog sink being selected, which no supplied file contemplates.

clauses.clause: When to define events vs spans vs span attributes vs plain log records; events may be emitted inside or outside an active trace context
clauses.note: The 'events can be emitted outside an active trace context' half is covered by LR:139-140 (outside-span logs may legitimately have no context). The choose-events-vs-spans-vs-span-attributes decision guidance is absent, which is acceptable given the skills do not author semantic conventions.

clauses.clause: Event name MUST uniquely identify the structure; event names MUST NOT include dynamic values; use attributes for per-occurrence identifiers; prefer fully qualified domain-specific names
clauses.note: I:1540 constrains span-name cardinality only. No file carries the event-name cardinality rule, and A:322 notices span.AddEvent used as structured logging without applying any naming constraint.

clauses.clause: Events MUST have Timestamp set to occurrence time; semantic conventions MUST NOT define ObservedTimestamp
clauses.note: The occurrence-vs-observation split and the instruction that ObservedTimestamp is collection time, not author-defined, both match.

clauses.clause: Semantic conventions SHOULD specify a default severity number and MUST NOT define a severity text
clauses.note: Binds semconv authors. The skills correctly treat SeverityText as a bridge-preserved source string (LR:85-86) rather than something to define.

clauses.clause: Event attributes MUST be documented; reuse existing attributes; avoid copying every span attribute; prefer flat attributes; include error.type for failure outcomes; document attributes that may be sensitive, expensive or especially large
clauses.note: The sensitive/large-attribute documentation duty is well covered by the privacy and limits rules. error.type on failure events and the avoid-copying-span-attributes preference are absent; both bind convention authors more than this repo.

clauses.clause: Semantic conventions MUST NOT define a Body value except a string display message of the event
clauses.note: Binds semconv authors. Importantly this does NOT forbid applications from using a structured Body; LR:95-97 correctly preserves structured values instead.

clauses.clause: Scope: semconv authors SHOULD follow it; also recommended for application developers and non-OTel instrumentations; this document does NOT apply to logging bridges
clauses.note: Precise match. LR:176-179 states the bridge exclusion and draws the correct consequence: do not force every bridged error to add EventName, change severity, emit a second event, or migrate existing span exceptions.

clauses.clause: Exceptions SHOULD be recorded as attributes on the LogRecord passed to Logger emit operations
Exception events emitted by instrumentations that also record spans for the same operation MUST be associated with the corresponding span context
clauses.note: LR:181 requires associating the actual operation context for newly selected instrumentation exception events, and the LOG-CONTEXT join rules supply the proof mechanism.

clauses.clause: Where supported, instrumentations SHOULD pass the exception instance to Emit rather than setting individual attributes
clauses.note: Tension handled deliberately rather than missed: LR:170 prefers the supported bridge/SDK exception mapping, while LR:188-189 forbids passing a raw exception and relying on truncation when policy restricts fields. That is a defensible privacy-first reading, not a gap.

clauses.clause: Instrumentations SHOULD record exceptions as events
clauses.note: Correctly scoped to newly selected instrumentation and explicitly not imposed on bridged records, consistent with the Development status.

clauses.clause: Instrumentations SHOULD NOT record artificial exceptions generated for unsuccessful status codes (e.g. FastAPI HTTPException, Spring ResponseStatusException)
Event name RECOMMENDED as operation + '.exception'; non-domain-specific handlers SHOULD use 'exception'
clauses.note: LR:178 correctly forbids forcing EventName onto bridged errors and LR:180 defers to 'the applicable conventions and stability' for new instrumentation, but the .exception naming form itself is never stated. Low impact given Development status.

clauses.clause: Severity SHOULD be provided on all exception events and set by expected impact: FATAL 21, ERROR 17, WARN 13, INFO 9, DEBUG 5, TRACE 1; semconv authors SHOULD NOT define TRACE
clauses.note: LR:181-182 'choose severity from impact' states the governing principle; the numeric anchors are already present in LR:86-87.

clauses.clause: exception.message and exception.type are each Conditionally Required (required if the other is not set, recommended otherwise); exception.stacktrace is Recommended; exception.message may contain sensitive information; exception.type MAY be unwrapped from an unhelpful wrapper
clauses.note: The field set, the sensitivity of message/stack, the allowlist discipline and the 'type-only is a legitimate policy' case are all covered. The conditional pairing itself (recording neither type nor message leaves the event under-identified) is never stated, and stacktrace's merely-Recommended level is implied by 'as applicable' rather than named.

clauses.clause: Migration: OTEL_SEMCONV_EXCEPTION_SIGNAL_OPT_IN with values logs and logs/dup SHOULD be introduced; default keeps span events; SHOULD maintain existing major version >= 6 months; MAY drop later; users may still route logs to span events at the SDK layer
clauses.note: LR:179 'Preserve bridge semantics and versioned opt-ins' and LR:178's prohibition on migrating existing span exceptions cover the intent. The specific variable name and its logs / logs/dup values are never given, so an auditor would not know what to look for in the environment.

clauses.clause: Instrumentations MAY add context attributes and MAY offer a config option to copy span attributes onto exception events
clauses.note: LR:190-191 protects unrelated application metadata from being stripped merely for not being an exception attribute, which is the correct handling of a MAY.

clauses.clause: Stacktrace representation is determined and documented by each language SIG
All server components MUST support none and gzip compression
Request size limits: server MUST enforce including after decompression (RECOMMENDED 64 MiB); client SHOULD limit and MUST NOT send oversized requests, SHOULD record the discard
clauses.note: Low applicability for an application-path audit: the client-side obligation is exporter-internal. Recorded for completeness rather than promoted to a gap, since an oversized-log-batch rejection would surface through the partial-success and drop accounting that LR:249-250 already requires.

clauses.clause: Client MAY wait per response; high-throughput clients SHOULD support concurrent unary calls; concurrency SHOULD be configurable
clauses.note: Covered in the sense that matters here: the skills require composing the whole-operation budget rather than assuming one in-flight request bounds it.

clauses.clause: On shutdown the client optionally waits for pending acknowledgements or an implementation timeout; the client implementation SHOULD expose an on/off option; undelivered data SHOULD be recorded
clauses.note: LR:355 requires 'a final log immediately before shutdown, with healthy receipt and bounded fault behavior checked independently', and J:833-835 notes CompletableResultCode.join does not cancel background delivery.

clauses.clause: Full success: server MUST return the Export response and MUST leave partial_success unset; empty requests SHOULD succeed
Partial success returns HTTP 200 with partial_success populated and rejected_log_records set; the client MUST NOT retry such a request
clauses.note: Both halves present: 'An HTTP 200 with OTLP partial-success rejected records is not full acceptance' and 'do not retry an entire partial-success batch as if all its records were rejected'.

clauses.clause: Retryable vs non-retryable failures; non-retryable MUST NOT be retried, MUST drop and SHOULD be counted; HTTP retryable set is exactly 429/502/503/504 and all other 4xx/5xx MUST NOT be retried; 400 MUST NOT be retried
clauses.note: Retry-ceiling reasoning, drop accounting and 503 probes are covered; the normative retryable/non-retryable status partition itself is never stated, so a fixture could treat a 400 as retryable without tripping any rule.

clauses.clause: Throttling: server SHOULD signal backpressure and the client MUST then throttle itself; client SHOULD honour Retry-After when present, otherwise exponential backoff; connection retries must have random jitter
clauses.note: Backoff duration and observed jitter are required evidence (J:821 records a measured 80-120ms for a 100ms base), but no file mentions Retry-After or gRPC RetryInfo.

clauses.clause: Default ports 4317 gRPC / 4318 HTTP; default log path /v1/logs; non-default paths MAY be configured; Content-Type MUST match and the server MUST echo it
clauses.note: Strongly covered and hardened beyond the spec: the skills treat 4317/4318 as conventional fallbacks only, require a non-default-port scenario (V:542-545), and forbid sending HTTP to a gRPC endpoint (I:1603).

clauses.clause: OTLP/JSON: traceId/spanId hex not base64; enums MUST be integers and enum name strings MUST NOT be used; receivers MUST ignore unknown fields; keys are lowerCamelCase; 64-bit ints including timeUnixNano/observedTimeUnixNano encoded as decimal strings
clauses.note: Covered incidentally but correctly: the Java runtime-proof query reads lowerCamelCase JSON keys (severityNumber, traceId, spanId) and N:670-672 warns against JavaScript Number round trips for 64-bit nanosecond timestamps, which is exactly the hazard this clause creates.

clauses.clause: Multi-destination exporting SHOULD use per-destination queuing, acknowledgement handling and retry over shared immutable data
clauses.note: The skills' concern is adjacent but different: they forbid a second cloud log destination entirely and keep logs local, so per-destination queue independence never arises for the log signal. Treated as scoped out rather than missed.

clauses.clause: Senders SHOULD NOT create empty envelopes; receivers MAY ignore them; forwarders MAY drop them
Encoders SHOULD ensure valid UTF-8 and producing invalid UTF-8 is a bug; decoders SHOULD replace invalid sequences with U+FFFD; intermediaries MAY pass through unvalidated
clauses.note: LR:225-226 requires non-ASCII input where the policy measures UTF-8 bytes and names 'valid UTF-8 truncation' as a Body overflow policy, and LR:223-224 tells the reader to check the installed SDK's Unicode behaviour before claiming broader handling. The replacement-character decode rule is absent but is a receiver concern.

clauses.clause: Known limitation: unacknowledged data is typically re-sent, so duplicates on the server are a deliberate accepted tradeoff; OTLP acknowledgements cover only one client/server pair and multi-hop end-to-end guarantees are out of scope
clauses.note: LR:240-242 refuses to promise durable or exactly-once delivery and explicitly labels the one-record acceptance check a healthy-path duplicate check rather than a network delivery guarantee.

clauses.clause: Implementations MUST NOT throw unhandled exceptions; API methods MUST NOT throw on misuse; the SDK MUST NOT throw for its own errors such as an unreachable exporter endpoint
clauses.note: Covered as the observable consequence: every language guide requires proving application progress and original-sink output continue during an exporter fault.

clauses.clause: API/SDK MAY fail fast at initialization but MUST NOT cause the application to fail later at runtime
clauses.note: I:1584-1585 forbids turning a log-only boundary conflict into an application startup exception or disabling the operator-owned trace/metric route.

clauses.clause: API methods accepting external callbacks MUST handle all errors; background tasks should run under a global error handler and should not fail permanently on internal errors
clauses.note: All four guides require testing error and cancellation cleanup paths on the owned async boundary, which is the application-side analogue of this clause.

clauses.clause: Self-troubleshooting telemetry should be easily enabled and filtered out by default; when a library suppresses an error that would otherwise reach the user it SHOULD log it per language conventions; SDKs MAY expose callbacks to handle self-diagnostics separately from application code
clauses.note: The 'separately from application code' half is the core of LOG-DIAGNOSTICS, and J:794-795 adds the practical warning that the installed SDK may log a failure below WARNING.

clauses.clause: SDK implementations MUST allow end users to change default error-handling behaviour for relevant errors
clauses.note: G:860-861 is notably careful: do not install another global handler when routing is already safe, and isolate the process if a test changes global error handling.

clauses.clause: On internal error an API expected to return non-null MUST return a pre-allocated no-op or default object
Implementations MAY offer these env vars but are not required to; if they do they SHOULD use these names and parsing; env configuration MUST have a direct code equivalent
clauses.note: LR:238-239 'use public APIs when a language does not consume those environment variables' is exactly the right handling of a MAY, and LR:206-212 forbids copying one language's configuration shape into another provider.

clauses.clause: The SDK MUST interpret an empty environment variable value the same way as unset
clauses.note: The classification tables do distinguish 'unset/empty' from an explicit value (J:118 'exporter unset/empty'), and A:225 keys on 'any nonempty generic OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS', so the empty-equals-unset semantics are respected in practice without being stated as a rule.

clauses.clause: Boolean env vars: only case-insensitive 'true' is true, implementations MUST NOT extend the set, everything else including unset/empty MUST be false, and a warning SHOULD be logged on fallback
clauses.note: No boolean log env var is in scope for these skills; OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER is an enum.

clauses.clause: OTEL_BLRP_SCHEDULE_DELAY 1000, OTEL_BLRP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT 30000, OTEL_BLRP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE 2048, OTEL_BLRP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE 512 and <= queue size; the span equivalents are OTEL_BSP_* with schedule delay 5000
clauses.note: LR:236-237 names OTEL_BLRP_* and states plainly that OTEL_BSP_* configures spans; every language guide repeats the do-not-substitute-span-options warning.

clauses.clause: OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT default 128 and OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT default no limit, with OTEL_ATTRIBUTE_* generic fallbacks; implementations SHOULD only offer env vars for truncation they implement
clauses.note: LR:197-199 names both variables as signal-specific 'subject to installed SDK support and generic fallback' and states that span limits do not configure log limits.

clauses.clause: OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER default otlp; values otlp, console, logging (deprecated), none; MAY accept a comma-separated list; otlp/stdout is Development
clauses.note: Thoroughly covered, including the harder cases: an ineffective none while a bridge still exports (A:338-340) and a generated none without an explicit operator opt-out failing default log acceptance (V:553-555).

clauses.clause: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED replaces all signals with no-op; OTEL_LOG_LEVEL default 'info' for the SDK internal logger; OTEL_SERVICE_NAME takes precedence over service.name in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES
clauses.note: Resource precedence is covered behaviourally by requiring assertion of effective resource attributes from collector data. OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is never named even though it would silence the log signal wholesale, and the SDK internal log level is approached via 'check the installed SDK's actual diagnostic level' rather than the variable.

clauses.clause: When OTEL_CONFIG_FILE is set, all other environment variables except those used for substitution MUST be ignored (OTEL_EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_FILE is the deprecated alias)
clauses.note: Highest-impact gap found: the entire logs classification in A:327-340 and all four exporter-precedence tables key on env vars that this clause can require the SDK to ignore.

clauses.clause: Unrecognised enum values MUST produce a warning and be gracefully ignored; unparseable numerics SHOULD warn and be treated as unset
clauses.note: SDK parsing obligation. Adjacent but distinct from the skills' rule that an unrecognised explicit exporter is preserved as operator-owned.

clauses.clause: OpenTelemetry cannot determine what is sensitive in your context; the implementer is responsible for compliance, protection, consent, storage practices, and for reviewing what instrumentation libraries emit
clauses.note: Treated correctly as policy-driven rather than universal: LR:182-183 says no policy permission to collect a message or stack means omit it, not enable capture for a test, and A:323-326 requires checking the final formatting path rather than only logger call arguments.

clauses.clause: Data minimization: collect only what serves an observability purpose, avoid personal information unless necessary, consider aggregation or anonymisation, review collected attributes regularly
clauses.note: J:146-147 'Never use * as the MDC allowlist' and LR:173-174 'truncation alone is not redaction' are concrete minimization rules.

clauses.clause: Collector-side protection is an offered route: attributes, filter, redaction and transform processors, where redaction deletes attributes not matching an allowlist
Hashing may not provide sufficient anonymization because hashes are reversible when the input space is small and predictable; truncation or prefix grouping offered as alternatives
clauses.note: The skills prefer omission and allowlists over transformation, so the hashing pitfall never arises as a recommended technique. No rule would catch an application that substituted a weak hash and claimed redaction, but the allowlist discipline makes that path unlikely.

clauses.clause: Sensitive categories are examples only and what is sensitive varies by situation: PII, credentials, session tokens, financial, health, user behaviour
clauses.note: The skills enumerate request, user, tenant, session, trace, raw URL, exception text and traceback as the surfaces to review, and consistently gate them on an explicit policy allowance rather than declaring them universally forbidden.

clauses.clause: All listed OTLP exporter configuration options MUST be available, and each MUST be overridable by a signal-specific option
clauses.note: The skills' whole generic-vs-signal-specific endpoint discipline rests on this clause.

clauses.clause: OTLP/HTTP endpoint MUST honor scheme, host, port and path and MAY ignore other URL components; default http://localhost:4318; gRPC default http://localhost:4317
Per-signal endpoint variables MUST be used as-is (root path / if none); only the generic OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT gets v1/logs appended; an SDK MUST NOT modify the URL in other ways
clauses.note: P:811-812 ('a compatible generic local endpoint is inherited with its non-default port and signal path') is exactly this construction rule, and I:1601 names the /v1/logs baseline.

clauses.clause: Exporter Timeout is the maximum time for each batch export including all request attempts and waits between retries; it starts when the batch export begins and MUST NOT be reset for each request attempt; it is distinct from connection or per-attempt timeouts; default 10s
clauses.note: Direct confirmation of LR:261-264. The 10s default was not recorded anywhere in the supplied files; the guides discuss 800ms/1000ms fixture policies instead, which is a fixture choice rather than a contradiction.

clauses.clause: Exporter Max Request Size default 67108864 (64 MiB) and Max Response Size default 4194304 (4 MiB)
clauses.note: Supersedes the earlier I2 'recorded not promoted' treatment: there are now concrete exporter-level defaults an audit could read.

clauses.clause: Protocol MUST be one of grpc, http/protobuf, http/json; SDKs SHOULD support grpc and http/protobuf and MUST support at least one; if only one it SHOULD be http/protobuf; default SHOULD be http/protobuf
clauses.note: I:1600-1601 names http/protobuf as the local baseline, matching the spec's SHOULD default, and I:1603 forbids sending HTTP to a gRPC endpoint.

clauses.clause: OTLP header environment variables use W3C Baggage key1=value1,key2=value2 form; semicolon-delimited metadata is not supported; all attribute values MUST be considered strings
clauses.note: The skills treat headers only as a credential-leak surface and never parse their format. Sufficient for their purpose; the format rule is not needed to detect a non-empty generic header.

clauses.clause: Transient errors MUST be handled with a retry strategy, and that strategy MUST implement exponential back-off with jitter
clauses.note: J:820-822 requires checking actual jitter and records a measured 80-120ms band for a 100ms base, which is the empirical form of this MUST.

clauses.clause: Each request attempt and wait between retries MUST be bounded by the remaining exporter timeout; any earlier caller deadline (span processor, log processor or metric reader) MUST take precedence; when either limit is reached the exporter MUST stop attempting, including waits between retries, and complete with a failure result
clauses.note: This is the single strongest confirmation in round 2. LR:263-264 ('an earlier caller deadline takes precedence') and LR:290-293 (keep exporter attempts, processor waits and caller lifecycle deadlines distinct) restate this clause almost verbatim, and LR:269-271 draws the correct consequence that a max attempt count is a ceiling an earlier deadline can cut short.

clauses.clause: Compression has no specified default value; SIGs may choose among supported options; supported values are none and gzip
clauses.note: No logging decision in the supplied files turns on compression.

clauses.clause: OTLP exporters SHOULD emit a User-Agent identifying exporter, language and version; MAY expose an option to prepend a distribution identifier
Insecure, certificate file, client key and client certificate options for transport security, each with signal-specific variants
clauses.normative: MUST be available; MAY be omitted where the gRPC client does not support insecure
clauses.note: The local-receiver log path in the supplied files is plain HTTP to localhost; TLS options never arise.

clauses.clause: All languages MUST provide a No-Op; No-Op components MUST NOT hold configuration or operational state; all No-op operations MUST accept all defined parameters, MUST NOT validate arguments, and MUST NOT return any non-empty error or log any message
clauses.note: A:238-239 and A:243-244 already require detecting no-op provider branches and classifying a signal as source-defined but inactive. The 'MUST NOT log any message' property matters because it means a disabled log path produces no diagnostic trace, which the skills never say.

clauses.clause: The No-Op Logger's Enabled MUST always return false
clauses.note: Completes the Enabled picture: a disabled Logger is a No-op whose Enabled is always false, so an Enabled-gated caller emits nothing at all.

clauses.clause: The standard output LogRecord exporter's output format is unspecified and can vary between implementations; documentation SHOULD warn users, with recommended wording stating it is for debugging and learning and not recommended for production
clauses.note: The skills treat any non-otlp exporter value, console included, as operator-owned and explicitly do not interpret it. That is a safe handling, but they never record that console output is format-unstable and production-discouraged, so an audit cannot advise on it.

clauses.clause: Where a language auto-configures a processor to pair with the selected exporter (e.g. via OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER), the standard output exporter SHOULD by default be paired with a simple processor
clauses.note: Directly contradicts an assumption the delivery rules rest on: LR:235 says 'Use the existing provider's batch processor', but on the console branch the spec default is a simple processor, so OTEL_BLRP_* queue and batch reasoning does not apply.

clauses.clause: A Resource can be associated with a LoggerProvider, and then all log records produced by any Logger from that provider will be associated with that Resource; the association cannot be changed later
clauses.normative: descriptive + MUST for traces, analogous for logs
clauses.note: The immutability of the association is precisely why the skills forbid building a second provider to change limits and require preserving the existing resource.

clauses.clause: The SDK MUST provide access to a Resource with at least the SDK-provided default attributes, and that resource MUST be associated with a TracerProvider, MeterProvider or LoggerProvider if another resource was not explicitly specified
clauses.note: Supports the skills' requirement that logs carry the same service resource identity as traces and metrics without the application restating it.

clauses.clause: The SDK MUST extract OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and merge it as the SECONDARY resource, so user-provided resource information has HIGHER priority
clauses.note: Precedence runs the opposite way to the intuition behind I:1077-1080. The skills' instruction to preserve operator resource values is achievable only by omitting those keys from code, because if the application sets them explicitly the spec says code wins.

clauses.clause: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES is a key1=value1,key2=value2 list; all values MUST be considered strings; , and = in keys and values MUST be percent-encoded; on any decoding error the entire variable value SHOULD be discarded and an error SHOULD be reported
clauses.note: A malformed value discards the whole variable, which would silently drop every operator resource attribute the skills rely on at I:1077-1081 and V:562-564.

clauses.clause: Merge: the updating resource's values win per key; Schema URL merge rules apply, and two non-empty differing Schema URLs is a merging error whose result is undefined
clauses.note: The per-key merge is covered by the merge-only-absent-keys rule and its focused resource-merge test. The Schema URL conflict case is absent and would make the effective resource undefined.

clauses.clause: Resource detectors MUST be separate packages from the SDK; failure to detect any resource information MUST NOT be considered an error, whereas an error during an attempt SHOULD be
The reserved service resource detector populates service.name from OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, SHOULD fall back to language or platform sources, and populates service.instance.id
clauses.note: service.name is central to the skills' shared-identity checks. The documented language fallbacks (for example spring.application.name or a JAR manifest) are never mentioned, so an audit could report a missing OTEL_SERVICE_NAME as a gap when a fallback already supplies the value.

clauses.clause: Entities, entity-aware detectors and the Resource Provider, including asynchronous descriptive-attribute resolution with identifying attributes resolved before first export
clauses.note: Development-status feature with no bearing on the supplied logging instructions; recorded so the omission is deliberate rather than overlooked.

clauses.clause: Resources are immutable; only creation, merge and retrieval operations are provided
Attribute requirement levels apply to the instrumentation library, and cover Log, Metric, Resource and Span attributes defined in semantic conventions
clauses.note: I:1126-1131 reasons in exactly these terms (required first, recommended only when a requirement depends on them), and LR:25-27 keeps author-level obligations off application code.

clauses.clause: Required: all instrumentations MUST populate the attribute; its presence can be used to detect that a telemetry item follows a convention

Conditionally Required: MUST populate when the condition is satisfied; the convention MUST clarify the condition; when the condition is unmet and the instrumentation can still populate it, it SHOULD use the Opt-In level
clauses.note: Resolves H9: exception.message and exception.type are each Conditionally Required on the other's absence, so a type-only allowlist is compliant and so is a message-only one, but recording neither leaves the event unidentified. The skills' allowlist rules never state that floor.

clauses.clause: Recommended: instrumentations SHOULD add the attribute by default if readily available and efficiently populated; MAY offer a configuration option to disable; those declining for performance, security or privacy SHOULD allow users to opt in
clauses.note: I:1128-1130 is more conservative than the spec SHOULD (it adds recommended signals only when an approved requirement depends on them, the value is accurately observable, and privacy/cardinality rules permit). That is a labeled tightening of a SHOULD, which the spec permits, not a misreading.

clauses.clause: Opt-In: instrumentations SHOULD populate the attribute if and only if the user configures them to do so, and instrumentation that does not support configuration MUST NOT populate Opt-In attributes; this level is recommended for attributes that are particularly expensive to retrieve or might pose a security or privacy risk
clauses.note: This resolves the optional-enablement question. V:64 elevates content/vendor fields to required acceptance 'even when OTel publishes them as Opt-In', which is consistent with this clause only because A:809-817 and V:66-69 first require an explicit configured capture policy; Opt-In means populate iff configured, and the capture-policy contract is that configuration. The elevation is scoped to the GenAI content domain and labeled, not applied to ordinary application logs.

clauses.clause: Performance suggestions: expensive operations such as DNS lookups, forcing route calculation or reading a response stream should be avoided by default
clauses.note: Mirrored on the logging side by the Enabled optimisation (B5), which exists for exactly this reason and which the skills do not mention.

clauses.clause: Naming applies to attribute keys and to Event names; every name MUST be a valid Unicode sequence; names SHOULD be lowercase, dot-namespaced, snake_case within multi-word components, and precise
clauses.note: I:1125 requires strict adherence to semantic conventions for span and metric naming and attributes, but the sentence does not mention log attributes or event names.

clauses.clause: Two attributes, two metrics or two events MUST NOT share the same name; different entity kinds MAY; conventions SHOULD NOT be removed but SHOULD be deprecated
Attribute names starting with otel. are reserved to be defined by the OpenTelemetry specification, and any additions to the otel.* namespace MUST be approved as part of the specification
clauses.note: Relevant because the skills already rely on spec-defined otel.* keys (otel.scope.*, otel.dropped_attributes_count) and because the Splunk HEC mapping in S26 introduces otel.log.* field names, so the boundary between reserved and inventable keys matters.

clauses.clause: Application developers should prefix company- or application-specific names with a reverse domain name or the application name, and it is not recommended to use an existing OpenTelemetry semantic convention namespace as a prefix for a new company- or application-specific attribute name
clauses.note: I:1130-1131 forbids inventing custom attributes where a convention signal exists, and LR:170-172 forbids exporting an exception under invented keys, but neither gives the positive naming rule for the custom log attributes an application legitimately needs.

clauses.clause: Attributes referencing external content: when values contain large, binary or sensitive data, pipelines or instrumentations may offload them and replace the attribute with a reference using a _ref suffix; the reference MUST have a corresponding base attribute, its type MUST be string and SHOULD be an absolute URI
clauses.note: An officially sanctioned third option alongside the skills' truncate-or-omit pair for oversized or sensitive content (LR:214, LR:226-231, I:1855-1856). Development status, so it must stay a capability lead.

clauses.clause: Attribute pluralization: singular for a single entity, pluralized with an array value type when it can represent multiple entities
log.iostream records the stream a log record was emitted to; stdout and stderr are well-known values and if one applies it MUST be used, otherwise a custom value MAY be used
clauses.normative: MUST (value choice) within a Development attribute
clauses.note: The skills distinguish stdout and stderr sinks extensively (A:318-320, I:1589-1593) but never name the attribute that records which stream a collected record came from.

clauses.clause: log.file.name, log.file.name_resolved, log.file.path and log.file.path_resolved describe the file a log record was emitted to
clauses.note: Set by file-tailing collection, which the supplied instructions deliberately do not own; they preserve the file sink rather than ingest it. Marked not applicable on ownership grounds, not overlooked.

clauses.clause: log.record.original carries the complete original log record and may contain large values; applications should configure the SDK attribute value limits, and instrumentations SHOULD additionally enforce an implementation-specific size limit before constructing or recording the value to avoid unbounded memory consumption; it MAY be added when the original was transmitted as a string and Body does not contain the same value
clauses.note: The underlying principle is covered by LOG-LIMITS, and the clause independently corroborates the skills' insistence that attribute limits alone are not a sufficient size policy: it tells instrumentations to bound the value BEFORE constructing it, which is the same pre-capture stance as I:1855-1856.

clauses.clause: log.record.uid uniquely identifies a log record; records sharing an ID are considered duplicates and can be removed safely, so two distinguishable log records MUST have different values; it MAY be a ULID or another identifier
clauses.note: Directly adjacent to the skills' heaviest theme. Duplicate prevention is enforced structurally (exactly one bridge per record) and verified by counting records; log.record.uid is the official per-record deduplication mechanism and is never mentioned.

clauses.clause: The event.name ATTRIBUTE is Deprecated: its value MUST now be set as the value of the EventName field on the LogRecord to indicate that the record represents an Event
clauses.note: LR:97-98 correctly treats EventName as the top-level field, so the skills are on the right side of this migration, but they never flag the deprecated event.name attribute an audit may still encounter in existing code.

clauses.clause: exception.escaped is Deprecated: it is no longer recommended to record exceptions that are handled and do not escape the scope of a span
clauses.note: LR:186 names error.kind and error.dump as excluded aliases; exception.escaped is a third, officially deprecated one that belongs in the same allowlist rule.

clauses.clause: code.file.path, code.function.name, code.line.number, code.column.number and code.stacktrace are Stable; code.stacktrace uses the same representation as exception.stacktrace
clauses.note: Call-site attribution is a normal part of bridged log records; S26 Appendix A maps journald CODE_FILE, CODE_LINE and CODE_FUNC and Zap caller onto these keys. The skills discuss preserving structured values but never name the stable code.* keys.

clauses.clause: code.filepath, code.function, code.lineno, code.namespace and code.column are Deprecated in favour of the dotted forms, with namespace folded into code.function.name
clauses.note: Concretely likely in Python, whose stdlib LogRecord exposes pathname, lineno and funcName; a bridge or formatter mapping those to the deprecated keys would pass every check in the supplied instructions.

clauses.clause: Appendix A maps logging-library call-site fields onto code.* log record attributes (journald CODE_FILE, CODE_LINE, CODE_FUNC) and leaves Zap caller as key TBD

OpenTelemetry SDKs SHOULD emit self-observability telemetry about their own behavior, including the state of processors and exporters; telemetry emitted during SDK startup and shutdown is best-effort because the recording SDK may not yet be initialized or may already be shut down
clauses.note: The skills require proving bounded diagnostics and observable failure, which is the same goal, but they reach it only through log-based diagnostic routing. The best-effort caveat also matters for LR:355, which asks for a final log immediately before shutdown.

clauses.clause: The SDK self-observability log instrument set is otel.sdk.log.created, otel.sdk.processor.log.queue.size, otel.sdk.processor.log.queue.capacity, otel.sdk.processor.log.processed, otel.sdk.exporter.log.inflight, otel.sdk.exporter.log.exported, plus the shared otel.sdk.exporter.operation.duration; all are Development and each is a recommended metric
clauses.note: This is the officially defined instrument set for exactly the evidence LR:249-250 and LR:355 demand (attempted, accepted, rejected, dropped, queue pressure). Development status and per-SDK support mean it must be offered as a capability lead, never as a required upgrade.

clauses.clause: otel.sdk.log.created counts log records submitted to an ENABLED Logger; a disabled Logger (LoggerConfig.enabled false) is a No-op whose records are not counted; every record submitted to an enabled Logger is counted even if later filtered or dropped by minimum severity, trace-based rules, a processor or the export pipeline, making this metric the top of the log delivery funnel; records never submitted are not counted, for example when a caller skips Emit after an Enabled check or an upstream logging library filters first
clauses.note: Independent corroboration of GAP-2 from a second source: the official funnel model is defined in terms of LoggerConfig.enabled, minimum severity, trace-based rules and the Enabled() check, three of which appear nowhere in the supplied files.

clauses.clause: otel.sdk.exporter.log.exported counts records whose export finished; for exporters with partial success semantics such as OTLP rejected_log_records, rejected records MUST count as failed and only non-rejected records count as success, with rejected SHOULD be used as the error.type value when no reason is available; if the exporter retries, the operation is finished only after the final attempt, each record MUST be counted exactly once per export operation, and intermediate failed attempts followed by a retry MUST NOT increment the counter
clauses.note: Strong independent corroboration. The accounting model the skills insist on (partial success is not full acceptance, do not retry the whole batch as if all records were rejected, receipt counts do not equal attempted calls) is the same model this metric formalises, including the rule that retried attempts must not be double counted.

clauses.clause: Per-language Logs signal maturity as published in the Language APIs and SDKs status table: Java Stable, Go Release candidate, JavaScript Development, Python Development; traces and metrics are Stable for all four
clauses.note: The four language guides and I:1564-1567 treat Python, Node.js, Java and Go as an undifferentiated set of supported logging stacks. The published Logs maturity differs sharply across exactly those four, which is the coarse-grained form of the capability caution the skills already apply at API level.

clauses.clause: Regardless of an API or SDK's status, instrumentation relying on semantic conventions marked Experimental may be subject to breaking changes
clauses.note: LR:40-41 ('Check individual development features rather than describing an entire language or exception convention as stable') is a precise statement of this warning, and A:230-232 plus I:1120-1121 handle the opt-in timing relative to imports.

clauses.clause: OpenTelemetry Python publishes Logs as Development while traces and metrics are Stable, and supports Python 3.10 and higher
clauses.note: Python carries the most detailed limit and bridge instructions of the four guides (P:887-927) while being one of the two Development-status log implementations, so the capability caveats there are load-bearing.

clauses.clause: The Data Model Appendix is explicitly NOT a spec; its examples are purely demonstrative and are not exhaustive or canonical, and exporter documentation should be consulted for exact details
clauses.note: LR:48 states that supplementary guidance does not add normative SDK requirements, which is the correct handling for this document too.

clauses.clause: Appendix B example SeverityNumber mappings: Log4j DEBUG 5, INFO 9, WARN 13, ERROR 17, FATAL 21; java.util.logging FINEST 1, FINER 5, FINE 6, CONFIG 7, INFO 9, WARNING 13, SEVERE 17; Zap Debug 5, Info 9, Warn 13, Error 17, Dpanic 18, Panic 19, Fatal 21; Syslog Debug 7 to 5, Informational 6 to 9, Notice 5 to 10, Warning 4 to 13, Error 3 to 17, Critical 2 to 18, Alert 1 to 19, Emergency 0 to 21
clauses.note: Confirms the exact numbers LR:86-87 asserts (DEBUG 5, INFO 9, WARN 13, ERROR 17) against the published Log4j and java.util.logging columns, and confirms LR:87's allowance that finer source levels use their documented range. Note the appendix is non-normative, so the numbers are examples consistent with the normative range rule in C7, not requirements in themselves.

clauses.clause: Appendix A Log4j mapping: Instant to Timestamp, Level to Severity, Message to Body, and all other fields to Attributes; the Zap mapping is equivalent with caller noted as key TBD
clauses.note: Corroborates the skills' insistence on preserving structured values as attributes rather than flattening a structured record into an opaque string.

clauses.clause: Appendix A Splunk HEC mapping: event to Body, time to Timestamp, host to Resource host.name, fields to Attributes, and on the reverse path SeverityText to Fields otel.log.severity.text, SeverityNumber to Fields otel.log.severity.number, TraceId to Fields trace_id, SpanId to Fields span_id and TraceFlags to Fields trace_flags
clauses.note: Notable given the repository's Splunk context: the published HEC correlation field names are the same trace_id, span_id and trace_flags that LR:142-145 already requires for non-OTLP sinks, so this example supports rather than complicates the existing rule. It is recorded because it is the one place where an official document shows a Splunk-specific non-OTLP log mapping.

clauses.clause: Appendix A ETW mapping: Level 0 LOG_ALWAYS is a filtering directive and not a severity, so SeverityNumber maps to UNSPECIFIED (0) rather than inventing a specific severity, while SeverityText keeps the original source name and the raw level is preserved in an attribute so the mapping stays reversible
clauses.note: The clearest published precedent for LR:89 ('Unknown severity may remain 0/absent; do not invent an ERROR classification'): an official mapping deliberately chooses UNSPECIFIED over a guessed severity and keeps the source value for reversibility.

dispositions.candidate: OTEL_CONFIG_FILE supersedes the environment variables the logs classification is built on — conditional on installed declarative-config support, and partial because substituted variables survive
dispositions.reason: Config classification previously used flat exporter/endpoint variables without resolving a supported active declarative loader. Resolve loader, substitutions and overlays first; unknown support stays unverified.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: LoggerConfig.enabled, minimum_severity, Logger.Enabled and the No-Op consequence are absent from the filtering and opt-out rules
dispositions.reason: Inspect effective supported SDK/logger enablement, minimum severity and trace filters. Keep optional native/direct-OTel cost guards separate from pipeline ownership. Default enabled is SHOULD true, not MUST.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: Collector-side sanitisation is not named as an owner for the general application-log path
dispositions.reason: Collector processing can satisfy an approved downstream boundary. It cannot close forbidden pre-SDK/pre-writer capture; the existing stricter privacy rule was already present. No weakening of that rule.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: Event-name cardinality rule is unstated
dispositions.reason: Selected semantic EventName cannot contain per-occurrence identifiers; only permitted varying data goes in attributes. Ordinary bridged messages need no EventName.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: Server-driven throttling signals are not distinguished from the exporter's own backoff
dispositions.reason: Distinguish server throttle instructions from client backoff under one whole deadline; verify supported exporter behavior instead of adding an app retry loop. HTTP400 is non-retryable.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: User-provided attributes MUST take precedence over exception-derived attributes
dispositions.reason: When the selected supported Emit API derives exception fields, user attributes win. Do not add an optional API or raw exception capture solely for this test.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: Event-to-span-event bridge processor (Development) adds a span event while the record MUST still continue down the pipeline
dispositions.reason: A selected event-to-span processor must continue the record; its absence does not require adding a new processor.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: SDK MAY provide a deep clone of ReadWriteLogRecord for asynchronous processors because the record is not required to be concurrent-safe
dispositions.reason: Only an owned custom asynchronous processor needs a verified safe snapshot/clone of mutable records. Built-in processors need no replacement; unknown public support stays unverified.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: Instrumentations SHOULD NOT record artificial exceptions raised for unsuccessful status codes
dispositions.reason: Development recommendation against instrumentation-generated artificial status exceptions excludes logging bridges and does not ban intentional application error logs.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: The attribute-discard diagnostic MUST be printed at most once per LogRecord, not per discarded attribute
dispositions.reason: Inspect SDK discard diagnostics: at most one per record, not one per dropped attribute. Do not replace SDK internals.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: Scope identity tuple should uniquely identify the emitter, and appenders should avoid setting Instrumentation Scope attributes because differing attributes on one Logger identity is an error
dispositions.reason: Preserve scope identity; conflicting scope attributes on the same logger are not new per-record fields.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: Syslog RFC5424 trace context via SD-ID OpenTelemetry
dispositions.reason: No syslog sink is selected. RFC5424-specific formatting is conditional on that path and does not belong in every language setup.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: OTEL_SDK_DISABLED replaces all signals with no-op implementations
dispositions.reason: An effective supported SDK_DISABLED opt-out is distinct from a missing bridge and does not disable an original native sink. A flat setting ignored by a file loader is not effective.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.

dispositions.candidate: exception.message and exception.type are each Conditionally Required when the other is absent, so at least one must be present, while exception.stacktrace is merely Recommended
dispositions.reason: For selected instrumentation exception events, require the permitted identifiable type/message pairing. If policy forbids both, report the semantic limitation without capturing them. Do not impose the floor on ordinary bridge messages.
dispositions.runtime_status: Not claimed for optional/unselected features. Current native scope is recorded separately.
